findings.title: Unauthenticated raw SQL error diagnostics and full stack traces exposed via inconsistent, non-graceful error handling (errorHandlingChallenge, id=27)
findings.analysis: GET /rest/user/security-question (no Authorization) with Accept: text/html returns 500/2946 B containing a raw HTML error page: Error: WHERE parameter "email" has invalid "undefined" value followed by a full Node/Express/Sequelize stack trace (query-generator.js:1770:13 and model.js:1140:47). On the identical request with Accept: application/json the application returns a different representation (500/1804 B, JSON error object with a "stack" field, sha256 20eec46aa7555e7df9a45e29f3ef1e662c629c0419b9e) — one failure, two error encodings, both leaking raw SQL diagnostics and internal stack frames. A second independent trigger, GET /redirect (no param), returns 500/2531 B TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'includes') with a full stack (sha256 020023ff4f9ae2b934531ecd4f7f04d012a055a23b67e99de52dbc3f7ec4ec48). The primary trigger is byte-stable across fresh reads (sha256 0b84d83c08cc28421da7b67c32d997676e490f8bd4016854f849200c2e11a90b). Any unauthenticated caller can observe these raw SQL/stack responses. This matches the challenge requirement: the error is neither gracefully handled (raw SQL + stack, not a sanitized message) nor consistently handled (representation-dependent encoding). Impact: disclosure of SQL dialect, module paths and line numbers, and a broad unhandled-exception exposure class on the same route pattern.
findings.false_positive_check: Benign behavior for this route class is a sanitized, consistent error response. A legitimate unknown route returns a graceful 404 body {"message":"Not Found","errors":[]} — no SQL diagnostics, no stack. The observed 500 raw-error pages are therefore not the application's normal graceful error path. The differential between Accept: text/html (raw WHERE + stack) and Accept: application/json (JSON error + stack) on the identical request proves inconsistency rather than a single benign exception. The response is unauthenticated and repeatable across fresh requests; the claim rests on structure (raw SQL WHERE text, stack frames, non-graceful encoding) rather than on any secret or sensitive data. A gracefully handled implementation would return the same normalized error form regardless of Accept header.

findings.title: Unauthenticated Prometheus /metrics endpoint exposes application telemetry including LLM usage counters and challenge-solved state (exposedMetricsChallenge, id=97)
findings.analysis: GET /metrics with no Authorization or credentials returns 200 text/plain with a Prometheus exposition-format body (~26141 B, sha256 100a183c15b9968b0393917ec4023c7d90ddb5d96b2fa8262fbb27aad7b96e48 at capture). The response includes juiceshop_llm_input_tokens_total, juiceshop_llm_output_tokens_total, juiceshop_llm_tool_calls_total gauges, http_requests_count (2XX/3XX/5XX), juiceshop_challenges_solved / juiceshop_challenges_total counters, process_*, nodejs_version_info and juiceshop_version_info=20.2.0. Secrets scan of the body reports zero secret-bearing lines; the exposure is operational telemetry, not credentials. Any caller — unauthenticated — obtains the full telemetry dump, including per-application LLM usage totals and the application's internal challenge-solved counters.
findings.false_positive_check: The endpoint requires no authentication: the same 200 response is returned without any credentials or session, and the content-type is text/plain Prometheus format with a predictable gauge structure (juiceshop_llm_* counters plus http_requests_count). Body bytes drift across calls because counter gauges increment, so the claim rests on structure and gauge presence rather than byte identity. A benign alternative would be either (a) a 401/403 for unauthenticated callers, or (b) a sanitized, non-incremental summary; the observed behavior is an unprotected Prometheus scrape target. The LLM usage counters and challenge-solved counters are application-internal state exposed to any caller, which is the precise exposure the challenge describes.
